literal: " The master of the house said: "The Emperor's gracious command: the envoy So-and-so has arrived, again proclaiming the central edict, inquiring concerning my clan name and lineage.
idiomatic: " The master of the house replied: "By the Emperor's gracious command, Envoy So-and-so has come and again reads the imperial edict, asking after my family name and lineage.

literal: My clan's daughter, born to her parents, is the surviving great-great-granddaughter of the late subject, the former Grand Minister of Splendid Brightness, Marquis of Yulou, Zhen; the great-granddaughter of the late subject, the former Inspector of Yuzhou, Marquis within the Passes, Yun; the granddaughter of the late subject, the former Administrator of Anfeng, Marquis within the Passes, Rui; and the surviving daughter of the late subject, the former Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, Zhun.
idiomatic: The daughter of our clan, born to her parents, is the last surviving great-great-granddaughter of the late Lord Zhen, former Grand Minister of Splendid Brightness and Marquis of Yulou; the great-granddaughter of the late Lord Yun, former Inspector of Yuzhou and Marquis within the Passes; the granddaughter of the late Lord Rui, former Administrator of Anfeng and Marquis within the Passes; and the surviving daughter of the late Lord Zhun, former Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary.

literal: On her mother's side, she is the maternal great-granddaughter of the late subject, the former Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Gou, and the maternal granddaughter of the late subject, the former Palace Attendant, Marquis within the Passes, Yi.
idiomatic: On her mother's side she counts as the maternal great-granddaughter of the late Lord Gou, former Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and the maternal granddaughter of the late Lord Yi, former Palace Attendant and Marquis within the Passes.

literal: She is seventeen years of age.
idiomatic: She is seventeen years old.

literal: I reverently receive the old regulations and solemnly obey the canonical ritual.
idiomatic: I receive the ancient statutes with reverence and observe the canonical rites with solemn care.

literal: " Next, the text of the board for Accepting the Auspice read: "The Emperor said: I consult the official of such rank, of such surname: human counsel agrees with the tortoise oracle; all declare it correct and auspicious; with reverence I follow the canonical ritual.
idiomatic: " Next came the board text for Accepting the Auspice: "The Emperor said: I consult the official of such rank and surname. Human counsel and the tortoise agree; all pronounce the match correct and auspicious. I shall reverently follow the canonical rite.

literal: Now I send the Bearer of the Staff of Authority, the Director of Ceremonies So-and-so, and the Director of the Imperial Clan So-and-so to accept the auspice according to ritual.
idiomatic: I now send the Bearer of the Staff of Authority, the Director of Ceremonies So-and-so, and the Director of the Imperial Clan So-and-so to accept the auspice by ritual.

literal: " The master of the house said: "The Emperor's gracious command: the envoy So-and-so again proclaims the central edict; the Grand Diviner finds it supremely auspicious.
idiomatic: " The master of the house replied: "By the Emperor's gracious command, Envoy So-and-so again reads the imperial edict. The Grand Diviner declares the match supremely auspicious.

literal: I, of a humble clan and low station, am burdened with anxiety and fear beyond bearing.
idiomatic: Our humble clan and low station are unworthy of such honor, and I am overwhelmed with anxiety and fear.

literal: I reverently receive the old regulations and solemnly obey the canonical ritual.
idiomatic: I receive the ancient statutes with reverence and observe the canonical rites with solemn care.

literal: " Next, the text of the board for the Betrothal Gift: "The Emperor said: I consult the daughter of the official of such rank, of such surname: she has the virtue of a model for mothers, a graceful and virtuous bearing, steadfast as mountains and rivers; fit to serve the ancestral temple and ever receive Heaven's mandate.
idiomatic: " Next came the board text for the Betrothal Gift: "The Emperor said: I consult the daughter of the official of such rank and surname. She has a mother's virtue, grace and modesty, steadfastness like mountains and rivers, and is fit to serve the ancestral temple and receive Heaven's mandate forever.

literal: With dark and light red silk, hides, silk, horses, sheep, cash, and jade disks—to manifest the canonical ritual.
idiomatic: Dark and light red silk, hides, silk, horses, sheep, cash, and jade disks are sent to display the canonical rite.

literal: Now I send the Bearer of the Staff of Authority, the Minister over the Masses So-and-so, and the Director of Ceremonies So-and-so to deliver the betrothal gift according to ritual.
idiomatic: I now send the Bearer of the Staff of Authority, the Minister over the Masses So-and-so, and the Director of Ceremonies So-and-so to deliver the betrothal gift by ritual.

literal: " The master of the house said: "The Emperor's gracious command: lowering marriage to my humble station, elevating it with the rank of Grand Duke, honoring it with canonical ritual, furnishing full ritual objects and written documents.
idiomatic: " The master of the house replied: "By the Emperor's gracious command, marriage is lowered to our humble house, yet raised with the rank of a Grand Duke, honored with canonical rite, and furnished with full ritual objects and written documents.

literal: I reverently receive the old regulations and solemnly obey the canonical ritual.
idiomatic: I receive the ancient statutes with reverence and observe the canonical rites with solemn care.

literal: " Next, the text of the board for Setting the Date: "The Emperor said: I consult the official of such rank, of such surname; taking counsel with dukes and ministers, divining with the great oracle and primordial tortoise—nothing inauspicious; fully following the canonical ritual.
idiomatic: " Next came the board text for Setting the Date: "The Emperor said: I consult the official of such rank and surname. After counsel with dukes and ministers and divination with the great oracle and primordial tortoise, nothing is inauspicious. I shall fully follow the canonical rite.

literal: Now I send the Bearer of the Staff of Authority, the Director of Ceremonies So-and-so, and the Director of the Imperial Clan So-and-so to request the date according to ritual.
idiomatic: I now send the Bearer of the Staff of Authority, the Director of Ceremonies So-and-so, and the Director of the Imperial Clan So-and-so to set the date by ritual.

literal: " The master of the house said: "The Emperor's gracious command: the envoy So-and-so again proclaims the central edict; the auspicious day is such-and-such, when the bride may be welcomed.
idiomatic: " The master of the house replied: "By the Emperor's gracious command, Envoy So-and-so again reads the imperial edict. The auspicious day is such-and-such, when the bride may be received.

literal: I reverently receive the old regulations and solemnly obey the canonical ritual.
idiomatic: I receive the ancient statutes with reverence and observe the canonical rites with solemn care.

literal: " Next, the text of the board for Welcoming the Bride in Person: "The Emperor said: I consult the official of such rank, of such surname; the year and month are auspicious, the auspicious day is such-and-such; follow ritual to welcome her.
idiomatic: " Next came the board text for Welcoming the Bride in Person: "The Emperor said: I consult the official of such rank and surname. The year and month are auspicious, and the auspicious day is such-and-such. I shall follow ritual to welcome her.

literal: Now I send the Bearer of the Staff of Authority, the Grand Tutor So-and-so, and the Grand Commander So-and-so to welcome her.
idiomatic: I now send the Bearer of the Staff of Authority, the Grand Tutor So-and-so, and the Grand Commander So-and-so to welcome her.

literal: " The master of the house said: "The Emperor's gracious command: the envoy So-and-so again proclaims the central edict.
idiomatic: " The master of the house replied: "By the Emperor's gracious command, Envoy So-and-so again reads the imperial edict.

literal: This month's auspicious day and hour—fully prepare ritual to welcome her.
idiomatic: On this month's auspicious day and hour, all ritual is prepared to welcome her.

literal: Grand dukes and clan ministers arrive together with deputy envoys; close retainers come in a hundred pairs.
idiomatic: Grand dukes and clan ministers arrive together with deputy envoys, and a hundred pairs of close retainers attend.

literal: I, a clan like ants, undeservedly receive this great ritual; anxious and trembling with fear, I reverently receive the old regulations and solemnly obey the canonical ritual.
idiomatic: Our clan is no more than ants, yet we undeservedly receive this great rite. Trembling with anxiety, I receive the ancient statutes with reverence and observe the canonical rites with solemn care.

literal: " Their prostrations accepting the edict were all as in the first responses.
idiomatic: " Their prostrations in accepting the edict followed the same form as the first replies.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took Empress Wang, the ritual was likewise observed.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took Empress Wang, the same rites were followed.

literal: For Presenting the Gift, Inquiring the Name, Accepting the Auspice, Setting the Date, and Welcoming the Bride in Person, one white wild goose and one white sheep were used in each, and wine and rice twelve bushels each.
idiomatic: For Presenting the Gift, Inquiring the Name, Accepting the Auspice, Setting the Date, and Welcoming the Bride, each rite used one white wild goose and one white sheep, with twelve bushels each of wine and rice.

literal: Only for the Betrothal Gift there was one sheep; dark and light red silk three bolts, crimson two bolts, plain silk two hundred bolts, two tiger hides, two million cash, one jade bi disk, six horses, and wine and rice twelve bushels each—what Zheng Xuan called the five geese and six rites.
idiomatic: Only the Betrothal Gift added one sheep, three bolts of dark and light red silk, two bolts of crimson silk, two hundred bolts of plain silk, two tiger hides, two million cash, one jade bi disk, six horses, and twelve bushels each of wine and rice—the "five geese and six rites" of Zheng Xuan.

literal: The regulations for jade scepters and horses and the numbers of ritual objects, compared with what was submitted in the Taikang era, again differed; the office has its annotations.
idiomatic: Regulations for jade scepters and horses and the tally of ritual objects differed again from the Taikang submission; the office keeps its own notes.

literal: In antiquity both marriage and capping had libation ceremonies; three libation texts by Master Zheng are fully preserved.
idiomatic: In antiquity both marriage and capping included libation rites, and three libation texts by Zheng Xuan survive intact.

literal: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year of Yuanjia, when Emperor Wen of Song's crown prince took a consort, the six-rite texts did not differ from those for taking an empress.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yuanjia 15, when Emperor Wen of Song's crown prince took a consort, the texts for the six rites were the same as those for taking an empress.

literal: All officials presented gifts.
idiomatic: All officials presented congratulatory gifts.

literal: On renxu of that month, a banquet was held in the West Hall of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate for the chief and deputy commanders of the two palaces' guards, the aides of the three offices of the Minister over the Masses, Northern Expedition, and Southern Suppression, the provincial commissioners of Yang, Yan, and Jiang, the secretaries and above of the seven kingdoms of Pengcheng, Jiangxia, Nanqiao, Shixing, Wuling, Luling, and Nanfeng, and all prefects of two-thousand-bushel rank in the capital—all were invited.
idiomatic: On renxu of that month a banquet was held in the West Hall of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate for the chief and deputy commanders of the two palaces' guards, aides of the Minister over the Masses and the Northern Expedition and Southern Suppression offices, commissioners of Yang, Yan, and Jiang, secretaries and above from the seven kingdoms of Pengcheng, Jiangxia, Nanqiao, Shixing, Wuling, Luling, and Nanfeng, and every two-thousand-bushel prefect then in the capital.

literal: It was also decreed that at this small gathering music and entertainers should be suspended, as the Grand Consort Cao of Linchuan was in mourning at the time.
idiomatic: An edict also suspended music and entertainers at this smaller gathering, because the Grand Consort Cao of Linchuan was then in mourning.

literal: In the eleventh month of the fifth year of Taishi, Emperor Ming, the relevant offices memorialized: "According to the records, since the Eastern Jin, for the crown prince's marriage the betrothal gift ritual used one jade and two tiger hides—it is unclear on what authority this was based.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Taishi 5, Emperor Ming, the relevant offices memorialized: "Since Eastern Jin, the crown prince's betrothal gift has used one jade and two tiger hides, but it is unclear what precedent this follows.

literal: Perhaps the tiger was taken for its fierce might and brilliant pattern, and jade to symbolize virtue and its warm luster.
idiomatic: Perhaps the tiger was chosen for fierce power and brilliant markings, and jade for virtue and warm luster.

literal: Considering that gui and zhang are the finest jades, leopard hide likewise carries brilliant splendor, and bear and buffalo are also auspicious emblems in marriage ritual—in taking symbols by category, they too should be used together; it is unclear why the transmitted texts omit them.
idiomatic: Gui and zhang are the finest jades; leopard hide is likewise splendid; bear and buffalo are also auspicious marriage emblems. By analogy they too should be used, yet the transmitted texts leave them out, and the reason is unclear.

literal: The Jin in the south lacked many ritual objects; later generations inherited this without time to investigate.
idiomatic: Eastern Jin lacked many ritual objects, and later ages inherited the gap without time to investigate.

literal: Now statutes and ceremonial badges are about to be fully restored.
idiomatic: Now statutes and ceremonial insignia are to be fully restored.

literal: One should take the classics as norm and examine the old canons.
idiomatic: The classics should serve as model, and the old canons should be consulted.

literal: For the crown prince's marriage now, should the betrothal gift ritual employ gui, zhang, leopard hide, and bear-and-buffalo hide or not?
idiomatic: For the crown prince's marriage, should the betrothal gift include gui, zhang, leopard hide, and bear-and-buffalo hide?

literal: Submit the matter to the ritual officers to correct in detail according to the classics.
idiomatic: Let the ritual officers examine the classics and correct the practice in detail.

literal: If they should be used, should each be one?
idiomatic: If they are to be used, should there be one of each?

literal: Or should two be used for each?
idiomatic: Or should there be two of each?

literal: " Doctor Pei Zhaoming argued: "According to the Rites of Zhou, for the betrothal gift: dark and light red silk bundled with paired hides.
idiomatic: " Doctor Pei Zhaoming argued: "The Rites of Zhou says that the betrothal gift consists of dark and light red silk bundled with paired hides.

literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary says: 'Bundled silk 〈missing in source〉 ten lengths.
idiomatic: Zheng Xuan comments: 'Bundled silk 〈missing in source〉 ten lengths.

literal: Paired means two.
idiomatic: 'Paired' means two.

literal: Two hides as court offerings—deer hide.
idiomatic: Two hides serve as court offerings: deer hide.

literal: ' 〈missing in source〉 The Jin crown prince's consort-taking ritual notes: 'with two tiger hides.'
idiomatic: 〈missing in source〉 The Jin crown prince's consort-taking protocol reads: 'with two tiger hides.'

literal: In the Taiyuan era, for a princess's betrothal gift, one each of tiger and leopard hide was used.
idiomatic: In the Taiyuan era a princess's betrothal gift used one tiger hide and one leopard hide.

literal: Was this because marriage ritual did not distinguish the order of kings and dukes, so tiger and leopard hides were taken to honor and elevate the affair?
idiomatic: Was this because marriage rites did not distinguish royal from ducal rank, and tiger and leopard hides were chosen to honor and elevate the occasion?

literal: Though tiger and leopard are patterned, they are not used in the betrothal gift ritual.
idiomatic: Tiger and leopard may be splendidly marked, but they are not prescribed for the betrothal gift.

literal: Bear and buffalo are auspicious, yet marriage canon does not reach to them.
idiomatic: Bear and buffalo are auspicious, yet the marriage canon does not include them.

literal: Though gui and zhang are fine, perhaps their use differs in each case.
idiomatic: Gui and zhang are splendid, but their use may differ from case to case.

literal: Now the imperial way is broad and bright, ceremonial norms shine forth; the heir apparent's betrothal should follow the classic injunctions.
idiomatic: Now the imperial way is broad and bright and ceremonial norms are clear; the heir apparent's betrothal should follow the classic injunctions.

literal: All eccentric errors should be examined and decided in detail.
idiomatic: Every irregular deviation should be examined and decided in detail.

literal: Though ritual ages differ and form and substance vary, Zheng is patriarch of the Ru school and has clear explanations; clinging to the letter with shallow views surely breeds doubt.
idiomatic: Rites change from age to age and form and substance differ, yet Zheng Xuan is patriarch of the Ru school and his explanations are clear; shallow literalism only breeds doubt.

literal: Furthermore, the Director of Ceremonies Assistant Sun Shen argued: 'The canon of betrothal gifts may be increased or reduced only as righteousness requires; each age in practice took the scholar's marriage as its model.
idiomatic: The Director of Ceremonies Assistant Sun Shen also argued: 'Betrothal gifts may be increased or reduced only as righteousness requires. Each age in practice modeled itself on the scholar's marriage.

literal: If gui and zhang are used, they equal bi disks in grade; the patterned glory of the leopard, in meaning, parallels the tiger's markings; bear and buffalo express auspice and entrust propagation.
idiomatic: Gui and zhang match bi disks in grade; the leopard's patterned glory parallels the tiger's markings; bear and buffalo express auspice and the hope of offspring.

literal: Now the heir's lofty betrothal, with ritual preceding far-reaching instruction—the beauty of hides and jade should be fully displayed.
idiomatic: The heir's lofty betrothal, with ritual preceding instruction far and wide, should display the full splendor of hides and jade.

literal: The rites speak of bundled silk and paired hides; then gui and zhang should number the same as bi, and bear, buffalo, and patterned leopard should each be two.
idiomatic: Since the rites speak of bundled silk and paired hides, gui and zhang should match bi in number, and bear, buffalo, and patterned leopard should each be two.

literal: ' The Chief and Concurrent Erudite of the Imperial Academy Yu He argued: 'According to the Etiquette and Ceremonial on the betrothal gift, it simply says dark and light red silk bundled with assorted hides.
idiomatic: ' Chief and Concurrent Erudite of the Imperial Academy Yu He argued: 'The Etiquette and Ceremonial on the betrothal gift says only dark and light red silk bundled with assorted hides.

literal: The Records of Ritual, Sacrificial Victims section, says tiger and leopard hide with jade bi—not made up in vain.
idiomatic: The Records of Ritual, Sacrificial Victims, says tiger and leopard hide with jade bi—not an empty invention.

literal: Then tiger and leopard hides clearly use two; gui and bi should remain as before, one each.
idiomatic: Tiger and leopard hides are clearly used in pairs; gui and bi should remain one each, as before.

literal: ' Comparing Shen's and He's two arguments without difference: now add one each of gui and zhang, two each of leopard, bear, and buffalo hide—He's opinion is adopted.
idiomatic: ' Shen's and He's views agreed on the whole. Gui and zhang were added one each, and leopard, bear, and buffalo hide two each; Yu He's opinion was adopted.

literal: " The edict approved.
idiomatic: " The edict approved the proposal.

literal: In the tenth year of Taishi, Emperor Wu of Jin was about to betroth and appoint three Ladies and nine Palatines.
idiomatic: In Taishi 10, Emperor Wu of Jin was about to betroth and invest three Ladies and nine Palatines.

literal: The relevant offices memorialized: "By ritual, the empress is betrothed with a grain-patterned gui; there is no system of gifts for concubines and attendant ladies.
idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized: "By ritual the empress is betrothed with a grain-patterned gui, and there is no prescribed gift for concubines and attendant ladies.

literal: " The edict said: "Appointment may follow Wei precedent.
idiomatic: " The edict said: "Investiture may follow Wei precedent.

literal: " Thereupon at the Hall front he sent the Bearer of the Staff of Authority, concurrently Director of Ceremonies, to invest the Ladies, and the Censor-in-Chief, concurrently, to invest the Palatines.
idiomatic: " Thereupon, facing the hall, he sent the Bearer of the Staff of Authority, who was also Director of Ceremonies, to invest the Ladies, and the Censor-in-Chief to invest the Palatines.

literal: In Han and Wei ritual, the princess resided in her own residence, and the man who married her came to that residence to complete the marriage.
idiomatic: Under Han and Wei ritual the princess kept her own residence, and the man who married her went there to complete the marriage.

literal: The Grand Minister of Works Wang Lang held this unacceptable; afterward it was reformed.
idiomatic: Grand Minister of Works Wang Lang judged this improper, and the practice was later changed.

literal: Whenever great envoys were dispatched to invest the empress, the Three Excellencies, cap the crown prince, or invest feudal kings, the Emperor all attended at the Hall front.
idiomatic: Whenever great envoys were sent to invest the empress, the Three Excellencies, the crown prince at his capping, or feudal kings, the Emperor always faced the hall in person.

literal: The ceremony: the Director of Music overnight set the metal-and-stone music of the four sides before the hall.
idiomatic: In the ceremony the Director of Music set out the four-sided metal-and-stone ensemble before the hall the night before.

literal: At the second mark after midnight on the clepsydra, Palace Attendants, attending ministers, Supernumerary Masters of Horse, Central Ushers, Staff Horse Lieutenants, and Tiger Braves, with plumed-head guards screening the line, all entered; the Five-Ox banners all entered.
idiomatic: At the second clepsydra mark after midnight, Palace Attendants, attending ministers, supernumerary Masters of Horse, Central Ushers, Staff Horse Lieutenants, and Tiger Braves entered with plumed-head guards screening the ranks, and all Five-Ox banners entered.

literal: The Commandant of Tiger Braves and the Superintendent of the Forest Guard divided duty at the inner steps and End Gate.
idiomatic: The Commandant of Tiger Braves and the Superintendent of the Forest Guard took their posts at the inner steps and End Gate.

literal: One Supervising Censor and one Usher each watched the End Gate.
idiomatic: One Supervising Censor and one Usher each kept watch at the End Gate.

literal: Prison Superintendents A and B divided duty at the eastern and western steps of Zhonghua Gate.
idiomatic: Prison Superintendents A and B took the eastern and western steps at Zhonghua Gate.

literal: At the third mark, the Attending Censor in the Hall reported opening the Hall Gate, the South Halting-Chariot Gate, and the Xuanyang City Gate.
idiomatic: At the third clepsydra mark the Attending Censor in the Hall reported the opening of the Hall Gate, the South Halting-Chariot Gate, and the Xuanyang City Gate.

literal: Military adjutants, Palace Attendants, Regular Palace Attendants, Attendant Masters of Writing of the Yellow Gate, and Attendant Masters of Writing ascended the hall and flanked the imperial seat.
idiomatic: Military adjutants, Palace Attendants, Regular Palace Attendants, Attendant Masters of Writing of the Yellow Gate, and Attendant Masters of Writing entered the hall and flanked the imperial seat.

literal: The Director of the Masters of Writing and those who should ascend the steps entered in order.
idiomatic: The Director of the Masters of Writing and all who were to ascend the steps entered in order.

literal: The Master of Ritual Conduct led the Grand Master of Ceremonies in to display the Nine Guests.
idiomatic: The Master of Ritual Conduct led the Grand Master of Ceremonies in and arranged the Nine Guests.

literal: At the fourth mark, the Palace Attendant reported: "External preparations are complete.
idiomatic: At the fourth clepsydra mark the Palace Attendant reported: "All external preparations are complete.

literal: " The Emperor wore the robe and cap of state, ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and sat at the Hall front facing south.
idiomatic: " The Emperor put on the robe and cap of state, ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and sat facing south at the hall front.

literal: The Usher came forward, bowed once facing north, knelt, and reported: "Grand Master of Ceremonies, your subject So-and-so, prostrate, reports: the multitude of ministers are in place.
idiomatic: " The Usher stepped forward, bowed once facing north, knelt, and reported: "Grand Master of Ceremonies, your subject So-and-so, prostrate, reports that the ministers are all in place.

literal: All is prepared with care.
idiomatic: Everything has been prepared with care.

literal: " The Palace Attendant proclaimed the imperial decision: "It may proceed.
idiomatic: " The Palace Attendant announced the imperial decision: "Proceed.

literal: " The Usher prompted the bow; all in attendance bowed twice.
idiomatic: " The Usher called for the bow, and all present bowed twice.

literal: The Grand Master of Ceremonies, with one bow declaring himself subject, raised his head and reported: "I request to perform the rite.
idiomatic: The Grand Master of Ceremonies bowed once as subject, raised his head, and reported: "I request permission to perform the rite.

literal: " The Palace Attendant proclaimed the imperial decision: "It may proceed.
idiomatic: " The Palace Attendant announced the imperial decision: "Proceed.

literal: " The Grand Master of Ceremonies raised his hand and said: "The rite may proceed.
idiomatic: " The Grand Master of Ceremonies raised his hand and said: "The rite may begin.

literal: " The Usher led the escorts, the envoys, and those who were to be invested in to take their bowing positions.
idiomatic: " The Usher guided the escorts, envoys, and appointees to their places for the bow.

literal: The music of the four sides began.
idiomatic: The four-sided ensemble began to play.

literal: As the bow was about to take place, the music stopped.
idiomatic: Just before the bow, the music stopped.

literal: When the rite was complete, they departed.
idiomatic: When the rite was finished, they withdrew.

literal: The office has its annotations.
idiomatic: The office keeps its own notes on the ceremony.

literal: In old times at the New Year, reed, rush, and peach branches were regularly set out and chickens were dismembered at the palace and the gates of the hundred temples to expel evil vapors.
idiomatic: In old times at the New Year reed, rush, and peach branches were set out and chickens were dismembered at the palace and at the gates of the hundred temples to drive off evil vapors.

literal: Han practice placed them in the midsummer month; there were peach pegs, but no dismembering of chickens.
idiomatic: Han practice set them out in midsummer; there were peach pegs, but no chicken dismemberment.

literal: Considering that Emperor Ming greatly restored exorcism rites, He Yan's discussion of exorcism sacrifice cites chicken victims for exorcism and smearing blood—dismembering chickens likely began in Wei.
idiomatic: Since Emperor Ming greatly restored exorcism rites, He Yan's discussion of exorcism sacrifice cites chicken victims for exorcism and blood-smearing; dismembering chickens probably began under Wei.
